title: Grant element of loans, by lender
description: How concessional each lender's loans are, as the grant element of each loan.
content:
- Grant element: the share of a loan's face value that is a gift, once repayments are discounted.
- Concessional: a loan with a grant element of at least 35%.
- Tenor: the years until the last repayment falls due.

title: Who the largest recipients were
description: The recipients that took the most bilateral aid in one year.
content:
The largest recipients in 2022 were:
- Ukraine
- Türkiye
- Afghanistan
- Syria
- Ethiopia

title: Emergency relief spending, 2012 to 2022
description: Each line traces one donor's humanitarian spending across the years shown.
content: Hover over a line to see the donor and the amount for each year.

title: Bilateral giving by member, 2023
description: Official development assistance from each DAC member in a single year.
content: Each bar is one member of the Development Assistance Committee.

title: Most recent figures
description: The most recent year each country has reported to the creditor reporting system.
content:
The table covers three kinds of flow:
- grants
- loans
- equity investments

title: Top 10 countries for health aid
description: The ten countries that receive the most aid for health in the year you pick.
content: Bars run from the largest recipient at the top to the smallest at the bottom.

title: Debt service as a share of exports
description: Payments on external debt divided by the money each country earns from exports.
content: Zambia spends more than a third of its export earnings on debt service, the highest share in the region.

title: Climate finance between 2016 and 2021
description: Finance that donors report as aimed at mitigation or adaptation.
content: Donors mark each project with the Rio markers, which score how central the climate aim is.

title: Spending on schooling, by stage
description: Spending on primary, secondary and higher education, split by donor.
content:
Basic education covers:
- early childhood
- primary schooling
- skills for young people and adults

title: Trend in aid to agriculture
description: How each donor's spending on farming, forestry and fishing moves from year to year.
content: Aid to agriculture fell by a fifth after 2020 as donors shifted money to the pandemic response.

title: Private money brought in by official finance
description: Money from private investors that official guarantees, loans and equity bring in.
content:
1. Guarantees: the share of private lending a guarantee covers.
2. Syndicated loans: the share the official lender arranges.
3. Direct investment: the private equity raised beside the official stake.

title: Country programmable aid
description: The part of aid that a recipient country can plan for, which leaves out costs such as debt relief and student costs.
content: Programmable aid made up 54% of bilateral aid in the latest year, its lowest share in a decade.

title: Recipients by income group
description: Aid to each recipient, grouped by the World Bank income classification.
content:
The chart uses four income groups:
- low income
- lower-middle income
- upper-middle income
- high income

title: Net financial flows into African economies
description: Money arriving in the region minus repayments flowing out, from official and private lenders.
content: Net flows turned negative in 2023 for the first time since records began.

title: Donor rankings
description: Each donor's place by total aid, with the option to rank by share of income instead.
content: Sweden, Norway and Luxembourg give the largest share of their income in aid.

title: Multilateral contributions, 2000–2023
description: Core funding from each donor to the multilateral system, by agency.
content: Pick an agency to see the donors that fund it.

title: How disbursements differ from commitments
description: A commitment is a promise to spend; a disbursement is money paid out.
content: The gap between the two lines is money promised but not yet paid.

title: Gender equality in aid
description: Aid screened against the gender equality policy marker.
content:
- Principal: gender equality is the main aim of the project
- Significant: it is an important aim but not the main one
- Not targeted: the project was screened and does not aim at it

title: The latest year
description: What donors spent in the most recent year of reporting.
content: Donors disbursed USD 16 billion to fragile states in the latest year.

title: Chinese lending to Africa
description: Loans from Chinese state lenders to African governments and state firms.
content: Loan records come from public contracts, government budgets and lender reports.

title: Aid per person, by recipient
description: Aid to each country divided by its population.
content: Small island states receive the most aid per person.

title: Refugee costs from 2015 through 2022
description: Spending by donors on refugees in their own countries, counted as aid.
content: Donors may count the first twelve months of costs for each refugee.

title: Untied aid
description: The share of aid that recipients may spend on goods and services from any country.
content:
Aid is tied when the donor limits the purchase to its own firms.
Partly tied aid allows purchases from the donor and from developing countries.

title: Aid to Ukraine
description: Bilateral aid from DAC members to Ukraine.
content:
Ukraine became the largest single recipient of aid in 2022:
- the United States gave the most
- Germany came second

title: Health aid by disease
description: Spending on HIV, malaria, tuberculosis and other diseases.
content: Use the legend to show or hide each disease.

title: Top donors to the Global Fund
description: Pledges to each replenishment of the Global Fund, by donor.
content: The United States pledged a third of the total at the last replenishment.

title: Budget support
description: Aid paid into a recipient's budget to fund its own spending plans.
content:
General budget support funds the whole budget.
Sector budget support goes to one sector, such as health.

title: LDC aid in 2021
description: Aid to the countries the UN lists as least developed.
content: Donors agreed to give between 0.15% and 0.20% of their income to these countries.

title: How the data are cleaned
description: Steps applied to the raw records before they reach the chart.
content:
The pipeline runs four steps:
1. drop duplicate records
2. convert to constant prices
3. map recipients to regions
4. sum by year

title: Arrears to official creditors
description: Payments that borrowers missed on loans from governments and multilateral lenders.
content: Arrears have doubled since 2019 and now exceed USD 10 billion.
